body.p: The above Amendments and these Remarks are in reply to the non-final Office Action mailed December 8, 2023. Reconsideration and allowance of the application in view of the foregoing amendments and in view of the remarks to follow are respectfully requested.
I. Summary of Examiner's Rejections

Claims 1-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112 as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter. Claims 1-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 because the claimed invention is directed to an abstract idea without significantly more. Claim 10 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Nagaraj et al. (U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2020/0253544A1; hereinafter referred to as Nagaraj) in view of Nierenberg et al. (U.S. Patent No. 8,666,484B2; hereinafter referred to as Nierenberg) and further in view of Abele et al. (PCT Application Publication No. W02004005895A1; hereinafter referred to as Abele).
II. Summary of Applicant's Amendment

By the present amendments, Claims 1-7, 9, and 10 are amended, Claim 8 is cancelled, and new Claims 11-15 are added leaving for the Examiner's consideration Claims 1-7 and 9-15. The Applicant respectfully submits that the proposed amendments contain no new matter. The Applicant respectfully reserves the right to prosecute any originally presented, canceled, or withdrawn claims in a continuing or future application.
III. Claim rejections under 35 U.S.C. 4112
Claims 1-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112 as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter.

In correcting the raised indefiniteness and antecedent basis issues, Claim 1 is amended to more clearly define a signal pre-processor comprising a first filter with a first filtering frequency, a second filter with a second filtering frequency; an epoch generator configured to generate an epoch signal containing epochs of i-second epoch duration each and 10% overlapping of consecutive epochs.
Claims 2-7, 9, and 10 are also amended to correct all indefiniteness and antecedent basis issues. Claims 8 is canceled, rendering their respective rejections mooted.
By the amendments, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 1-7 and 9 are clear and thus the claim rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112 should be withdrawn.
IV. Claim rejections under 35 U.S.C. 101
Claims 1-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 because the claimed invention is directed to an abstract idea without significantly more.
Claim 1
Claim 1 as amended defines:
A device for assessing anesthesia of an animal subject in real-time from
electroencephalography (EEG) measurements of the animal subject during application of anesthesia, the device comprising:

a signal pre-processor comprising a first filter with a first filtering frequency, a second filter with a second filtering frequency, and a down-sampler to pre-process sequentially an incoming measured EEG signal from the EEG measurements of the animal subject;
wherein the pre-processing comprises:
removing unwanted signals and noise from the incoming measured EEG signal using the first filter and the second filter to generate a filtered
incoming measured EEG signal; and
down-sampling the filtered incoming measured EEG signal by the down-sampler to generate a down-sampled filtered incoming measured
EEG signal;
an epoch generator configured to generate an epoch signal containing epochs of 1-second epoch duration each and 10% overlapping of consecutive epochs;
wherein the epoch generator comprises a two-input multiplexer, an
address generator, and a memory;
wherein the two-input multiplexer receiving is configured to:
receive the down-sampled filtered incoming measured EEG signal,
a feedback of the epoch signal, and a selector input from the address
generator; and
generate a multiplexer output from the down-sampler output signal or the feedback of the epoch signal based on the selector input;
wherein the address generator comprises:
a slow counter configured to generate write addresses, and count from a slow counter start count to a slow counter end count in repeating
slow count cycles; and
a fast counter configured to generate read addresses, and count from a fast counter start count to a fast counter end count in repeating fast
count cycles that starts after each of the slow count cycles;
wherein the slow counter is further configured to repeat each of the slow
count cycles after each of the fast count cycles;
wherein the fast counter is further configured to repeat each of the fast
count cycles after each of the slow count cycles;
wherein the address generator is further configured to:
generate the selector input to the multiplexer to generate the multiplexer output from the down-sampler output signal during each of the
slow count cycles and from the feedback of the epoch signal during each
of the fast count cycles;
wherein the memory is configured to:
receive the multiplexer output, the write addresses, and the read addresses;
store the received multiplexer output according to the received write addresses; and
output a memory output data according to the received read addresses;
wherein the epoch signal being the memory output data;
a feature extractor configured to:
receive the epoch signal from the epoch generator;
extract a derivative feature of the received epoch signal by computing a
mean of accumulated squared-differences among the epochs in the received epoch
signal; and
extract a variance feature of the received epoch signal by computing a
square root of an average squared-deviation of the epochs in the received epoch
signal;
a classifier configured to:
perform a feature mapping on the derivative feature and the variance
feature; and
set a decision boundary from output of the feature mapping to generate a
classifier output, the classifier output being either that the animal subject being
awake or anesthetized or that the animal subject being awake or anesthetized;
and
a predictor comprising a predictor circuit configured to:
accumulate a plurality of the classifier's outputs;
compute a decision value effrom the accumulated classifier's outputs; determine a level of anesthesia of the animal subject from the decision
value; and
predict the animal subject's anesthesia condition from a plurality of
determined levels of anesthesia of the animal subject.

In the Office Action, it was alleged that Claim 1 recited the abstract ideas of mathematical process and mental processes under Step 1 Prong 1 of the subject matter eligibility test. The Applicant respectfully disagrees. Claim 1 as amended defines a device for assessing anesthesia of an animal subject in real-time from EEG measurements of the animal subject during application of anesthesia. The device, as described with exemplarily

embodiments in the Specification, is implemented with specially configured electronic components, i.e., FPGAs. It is an optimized complete system on chip circuit design. Further, because the specific use and application (assessing the anesthesia condition of an animal subject) of the claimed invention mandate real-time measurement of signals, processing of data, and computation of assessment results, none of the steps can be performed by human. Therefore, the Applicant respectfully submits that invention as claimed in the amended Claim 1 is a patent-eligible subject matter.

In the Office Action, it was alleged that Claims 1-10 do not include additional elements that integrate the mental process or the mathematical process into a practical application under Step 1 Prong 2 of the subject matter eligibility test. By the amendments to Claim 1, Claim 1 as amended now more clearly defines a device for assessing the anesthesia condition of an animal subject in real-time from EEG measurements of the animal subject during application of anesthesia, which comprises not only a signal pre- processor, an epoch generator, but also a feature extractor, a classifier, and a predictor for predicting the animal subject's anesthesia condition from an accumulation of specifically processed and transformed EEG measurement data.

Prior to the present invention, real-time assessment of an animal subject's anesthesia condition during an application of anesthesia is at best the anesthesiologist's guess work based on extrinsic measurements such as blood pressure, heart-rate, change in respiratory patterns, ability to respond to verbal commands, eyelash reflex, pupillary responses, etc. with no systematic approach. Thus, the invention as claimed in the amended Claim 1 provides a significant advancement to the state of the art.

In the Office Action, it was alleged that Claims 1-10 do not include additional elements that are sufficient to amount to significantly more than the judicial exception under Step 2B of the subject matter eligibility test. By the amendments to Claim 1, Claim 1 as amended more clearly defines a signal pre-processor, which comprises a first filter with a first filtering frequency, a second filter with a second filtering frequency, and a down-sampler to pre-process sequentially an incoming measured EEG signal from the EEG measurements of the animal subject. In the amended Claims 2 and 3, it is further defined that the first filter is configured with the first filtering frequency for compensating a power- line interference of the incoming measured EEG signal; and the second filter of the signal pre-processor is configured with the second filtering frequency being comparable to an

average frequency of a wide electroencephalography frequency region of the incoming measured EEG signal. While simple noise filtering techniques are well known in the art of electronic signal processing, using two filters with two different filtering frequencies to filter different types of noise in applications involving EEG measurements is not routinely done.

Further, the use of an epoch generator configured to generate an epoch signal containing epochs of 1-second epoch duration each and 10% overlapping of consecutive epochs, for which one of the purposes is to create a sliding window to divide each EEG channel into short-overlapped epochs as an optimal design for lower resources consumption, the smallest possible memory usage, and increased processing speed is not routinely done.

The Applicant submits that at least the aforementioned elements, without limitation, are necessary and significant due to the strict requirements of the real-time and in-field use of the claimed invention (assessing the anesthesia condition of an animal subject in real- time).
Therefore, the claims as amended now meet the requirements of the subject matter eligibility test, reconsideration therefore is respectfully requested.
Claims 2-7 and 9

Claims 2-7 and 9 are not addressed separately, but it is respectfully submitted that the claims are allowable as depending from an allowable independent claim, and further in view of the comments provided above. Reconsideration thereof is respectfully requested.
Claim 10

Claim 10 is not addressed separately, but it is respectfully submitted that Claim 10 as amended defines features that are substantially similar to those of Claim 1 as amended. As such, in view of the comments provided above, the claim should also be allowable. Reconsideration thereof is respectfully requested.
V. Claim rejections under 35 U.S.C. &103
Claim 10 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Nagaraj in view of Nierenberg and further in view of Abele.
Claim 10
Claim 10 as amended defines:
A method for determining depth of anesthesia (DOA) of an animal subject in real- time from electroencephalography (EEG) measurements, the method comprising:
detecting and measuring an EEG signal of the animal subject using an EEG electrode;
filtering the EEG signal to remove unwanted signals and noise;
down-sampling the filtered EEG signal for reducing data size and accelerating
subsequent processing without losing essential features of the EEG signal for subsequent
classification;
generating from the down-sampled EEG signal an epoch signal containing
epochs of 1-second epoch duration each and 10% overlapping of consecutive epochs;
extracting a derivative feature of the epoch signal by computing a mean of accumulated squared differences among the epochs in the epoch signal;
extracting a variance feature of the epoch signal by computing a square root of an average squared deviation of the epochs in the epoch signal;
mapping the derivative feature and the variance feature to determine a
classification boundary, followed by using an output of the mapping to determine a sigmoid function as a decision boundary between awake and anesthetized state comprising:
if the mapping output value is lower than 0.5 or 50%, a classifier output is
set to that the animal subject being awake during a time duration of the epochs;
otherwise, the classifier output is set to that the animal subject being anesthetized
during a time duration of the epochs; and

accumulating a plurality of the classifier outputs of consecutive awake and anesthetized epochs, respectively generate a prediction output of a likelihood the animal subject being awake or anesthetized in a successive epoch.

In the Office Action, it is alleged that although Nagaraj has not, Nierenberg teaches overlapping one EEG signal with a preceding EEG signal. Claim 10 as amended now more clearly defines the feature of generating from the down-sampled EEG signal an epoch

signal containing epochs of 1-second epoch duration each and 10% overlapping of consecutive epochs. The Applicant submits that none of the cited references and the combinations thereof has disclosed, taught, or suggested the feature.

In the Office Action, it is also alleged that although the combination of Nagaraj and Nierenberg has not, Abele teaches mapping the derivative and variance features to determine a classification boundary. Claim 10 as amended now more clearly defines the feature of mapping the derivative feature and the variance feature to determine a
classification boundary,followed by using an output of the mapping to determine a sigmoid

function as a decision boundary between awake and anesthetized state comprising: if the mapping output value is lower than 0.5 or 50%, a classifier output is set to that the animal subject being awake during a time duration of the epochs; otherwise, the classifier output is set to that the animal subject being anesthetized during a time duration of the epochs.

In addition, Claim 10 as amended now also more clearly defines that the derivative feature is extracted by computing a mean of accumulated squared differences among the epochs in the epoch signal; and the variance feature is extracted by computing a square root of an average squared deviation of the epochs in the epoch signal. The Applicant submits that none of the cited references and the combinations thereof has disclosed, taught, or suggested the features as defined in Claim 10 as amended.

Furthermore, the Applicant respectfully submits that Nagaraj has not disclosed, taught, or suggested the presently claimed invention. Nagaraj discloses a method for determining the DOA of a human subject, while presently claimed invention is a method for determining the DOA of an animal subject. The sedation methodology, technique, anesthetic agent, and EEG recording are entirely different between human and animal subjects, leading to different brain dynamics and EEG signatures.

For example, one of the prominent aspects of anesthetic agents is that the uses of different sedative drugs produce different EEG signatures. With humans, PropofolTM, SevofluraneTM, DexmedetomidineTM, and so on are usually used for human anesthesia. In contrast, IsofluraneTM is widely used on animals as an inhalation anesthetic agent, which cannot be used on humans as it produces severe side effects on human subjects. The EEG electrodes used on animals and humans are also very different. One is to be attached to the scalps of the human subjects, while the other may be screwed into the skulls of small animals, such as mice.

Nagaraj discloses a method that is based on logit transform and correlation to have a continuous sedation level estimation (Nagarj, para. [0080] - [0081]), which only relies only on the current epoch (of length of 4 second) for the classifier's decision. In contrast, the presently claimed invention includes a prediction mechanism based on accumulating classifier outputs for consecutive epochs. Also, the presently claimed invention's prediction mechanism relies on the epochs of length of only 1 second, thus faster, while maintaining high accuracy.

Nagaraj discloses a method that is based on down-sampling the EEG signals to 250Hz and filtering the EEG signals within the range of 0.5 - 25Hz. Meanwhile, the presently claimed invention includes a down-sampler to 500 Hz and low pass filter within the range 0.1 - 250 Hz. The high frequency oscillations, namely Gamma band (25-250 Hz), play a significant role in distinguishing between the awake and sedated states wherein the critical features between awake and anesthesia states are mainly located within high frequency oscillations. In Nagaraj's disclosure, Gamma band oscillations are totally disregarded.
New Claims 11-15

The Applicant respectfully submits that the cited references have not disclosed, taught, or otherwise suggested the features of the invention claimed in the newly added Claims 11-15. Notwithstanding the above, it is respectfully submitted that the claims are allowable as depending from an allowable independent claim. Reconsideration thereof is respectfully requested.
VI. Conclusion

In view of the above amendments and remarks, it is respectfully submitted that all of the claims now pending in the subject patent application should be allowable, and reconsideration thereof is respectfully requested. The Examiner is respectfully requested to email or telephone the undersigned if she can assist in any way in expediting issuance of a patent.
Respectfully submitted,
